tips.comment: Choice of 13 pro tipsters on the Racing Post card, William Haggas (SR 24%) trained Sea The Stars colt improved on first two runs when second over 1 mile at Windsor a month ago. That's clearly the best run on form going into this four runner maiden. Tom Marquand (SR 19%) rides. The step up in trip to ten furlongs looks sure to suit.

Latest triumph at Thirsk in April. A solid 6th in a handicap at York 24 days ago. High on the list of contenders, even though this represents a class increase, the 4-year-old is advancing and he has not reached his full potential. Jockey Fentiman, utilising a 5lb claim will be in contention.

The 5yo is a previous 6f C/D winner and is in good form. Only beaten just over a length last time out in a quality £39K handicap despite having a rotten passage. He’s better judged when winning his previous race, a useful 16 runner £31K handicap, winning a shade cosy by 1L+ - solid form. This race is not as strong and there are question marks against quite a few of these rivals.

Backing Rohaan, the 7-year-old Mayson gelding trained by David Evans, in tomorrow’s Pontefract Park Silver Sprint Trophy (6f, Class 2). He arrives in solid nick after a consistent spell on all??'weather this spring, including a 2nd at Southwell in February and a 4th at the same venue in March, all over 6f??'showing he remains effective and well-handled on AW . His most recent run back on turf returned a 3rd of 17 at Newbury on 12 June, demonstrating he retains his finishing touch over the summer surface .
Rated 84 and drawn to benefit from a decent tempo in this competitive eight-runner field, Rohaan combines fitness, course­ versatility, and proven class. Trainer David Evans has struck gold with him over this trip before, and his well-rounded record??'highlighted by top??'class sprint handicaps and group??'level attempts??'suggest he’s no surprise contender off his current mark.

Badri ran a very good third of eleven at Epsom on his penultimate start and ran a better race than the bare result suggests when under three lengths eighth at Newcastle. I thought he wasn't pushed too much on both starts, especially the Newcastle run. This is only his second turf run this year, and I think we could have a result here with Tom Marquand having his first ride on him.

Aleezdancer last won in a C2 in May last year. It has taken until May this year to drop to that last winning mark, with that last win being when third up after a break. Today is third up after a break and 4 lbs lighter than that last win.

City House looks a nice each way shout here. I would ignore the last time out run as it was a very difficult race on its second return run in the UK. This is calmer waters. Running off top weight looks better suited for this track as well. Expecting a big run.
Clearly doesn't like soft ground, and even still, hasn't been running that badly. Now dropped down another 4 lbs, and with better ground, I'll take 18/1.

Paladin won in December at the end of last term on the AW and came back last month and won again on turf, this time on GF. I would always expect more when second up after a break, especially as only up 2 lbs for that last win. Worth a go.
Dropping down the weights and has stall 1 with Danny T on board. Goes well fresh and will enjoy slightly firmer ground so well worth an e/w bet!

Run well in defeat twice recently with a 3rd at Lingfield and 2nd at Bath when trying the mile for the first time. Trainer is in decent form currently, and a better run is expected now that stamina is proven.

For me, this horse's 3rd in a maiden at Kempton on debut, when slowly away and making up ground late on over a furlong shorter, is a piece of form which puts him well ahead of this opening handicap mark. He's run 2 good races since too, but it's always going to be about getting a good handicap mark, and it looks to be mission achieved here. The first-time booking of Tom Marquand catches the eye too. He looks to have a serious chance here.

Backing Riyadh Gem, the 3-year-old Oasis Dream colt trained by Archie Watson, in tomorrow's Go Racing Bet With Jayne Handicap over 1m 6 y at Pontefract. He arrives in good nick following consistent runs this spring, including a fine win on Wolverhampton’s Tapeta in April, and two solid turf efforts: third at Chelmsford on June 5 and fourth at Ripon on June 19, where he handled 1m 1f well under Andrew Mullen .
That progression on both AW and turf shows versatility, and his current rating of 74 looks fair. With nine declared runners, this smaller field should suit jockey tactics??'especially on a galloping mile such as Pontefract’s. Expect Riyadh Gem to settle handy, track the leaders, and deliver a strong finish along the home straight.
His profile??'race-fit, adaptable, and in form??'makes him stand out at likely odds of 8/1??'12/1, offering strong each-way value.

SEED INVESTOR is still a maiden but looks potentially well-weighted based on the run at Doncaster in April, which came over the mile, in this grade and from this mark. Off colour the last twice, which is a concern, but is well drawn and will have a pace to aim at. Each-way claims if we get the horse that ran at Donny.

This is a very open sprint handicap. However, it might pay to stick with the very in-form Match Play, who won nicely here last time. The stable has hit top form of late, so everything looks set for a good run again.

C&D triumphed in the last race of the previous season, but did not improve upon reappearance, finishing 5th in a handicap at Thirsk 21 days ago. There are some uncertainties to address now, but trainer Julie Camacho may have the solutions. She generally performs well when entering only one runner at a flat meeting and has brought in Kiely Marshall to ride, who has won once and placed 3 times in his 8 races here. I think placing an each-way bet at 11/1 could return a small profit.

Soprano won a fillies listed event back in March, and the only run since was a G2 last month at the back of the pack. But she will be all the better for that run and worth another shot back in today's company.
Royal Dress underperformed at Epsom when behind Sparks Fly but Pontefract's stiff mile should suit her better and she should get her revenge.
If Charlotte's Web can reproduce her all-weather form now back on turf, she would hold every chance. She should certainly be involved in the finish here today if she can.
Francophone performs quite well on good going and is worth an each-way. Has won over this distance in a Group 1 before, and this jockey and trainer work well together. Each-way possibilities.

Has mostly been running in Group 3 & Listed races over the last 2 seasons but only career win came in 2nd race in class 5 maiden at Carlisle over 9f . Has been placed once in Group race getting her black type when finishing 3rd in Group 3 Atalanta Stakes over 8f at Sandown last August . Her last 3 runs have come at 8.5f at Epsom where course found her out & 2 runs over 10f on turf & all weather so drop back to 8f today should help her fair better .

Julia Augusta ran better than the bare result last time and now drops into slightly calmer waters. She has a decent back form in stronger company than today's competitors and remains on a workable mark. This looks a realistic spot, and if she gets a decent position early on, her stamina and class edge can come into play. I think she's a classy type with potential - underestimated in the market.

Cheshire Dancer has obviously got to improve to have a chance with most of the other runners here and is 23 lbs worse off than the highest rated here. Her trainer, Hugo Palmer, is not exactly flying either, but I feel she is coming into form and will show massive improvement. Most of the runners have disappointed their connections, but Cheshire Dancer ran better than ever to finish 3rd at Ascot recently and won at Leicester previously, so is in great heart.

Tropical Island was not bad last time out when fourth in a listed run on the AW. I am pinning my hopes on her returning to turf and it being a bit firmer underfoot, having had her last two wins on good EW.

Vicario ran a huge race last time out at York in a hot handicap. This is a big step up in class; however, there are a lot of good rivals in the field. But it's always worth the risk. I think if the trip suits her, we could sneak into the places here at a big price with Shoemark retaining the ride.

Highly promising gelded son of Ulysses & Muqantara ( Dam's sire First Samurai ) who returned to action on the 13th of May 2025 on his handicap bow and has been a whole different proposition since returning to action winning on his handicap debut and staying on with real promise on the occasion was last seen at Doncaster 32 days ago where finishing a respectable 2nd/7 and arrives here operating on an unchanged mark of 67 and it is very well possible Sir Mark Prescott's interesting looking project has a lot more in the locker and a mark of 67 underestimates him in my point of view as we are yet to see the finish article and this rapidly improving sort is likely to put up a bold showing here the blinkers are applied for the first time and they can have a positive effect jockey P Mulrennan takes the ride and can give Analogical a promising ride here at Pontefract . Respected .
Neck at recent mark, starting to run into form with its new mark on 3rd run. Rivals today are all on new marks, yet to show change of form.

Supreme Dancer runs in his first handicap race today. His most recent run was in a class two race where he finished sixth. What has happened since that race is interesting. The runners that finished first, second, third and fourth in that race have all gone on to win a race. The form looks strong. Now, Supreme Dancer runs in his first handicap race and has a handicap mark of 61. That appears to be very low and with a clear run Supreme Dancer can win his first race today.

Baggot Street was not bad on handicap debut last week when third and stepping up to 7f. But she lost the plot on the run in, and I think the return to 6f today and dropping to C6 could bring her back in the money.

Popty Ping disappointed when backed into favourite last time out, but it's interesting the yard have kept her in here as they clearly think she's in good shape. So, she looks worth backing if given the once over and deciding to run again today.
This horse achieved an RPR of 74 on its last run before receiving a mark and with that mark being 64 it looks thrown in.

Smith's last seven wins have come at Lingfield on the all-weather, but he did win one on turf in his early career at Windsor. He should still be competitive off a mark of 47 despite his advancing age.
Amestris was a good improved second when last out, when second up after wind surgery, and goes again off the same mark with Oisin this time. So, I would expect to see more improvement again.

Ran with credit off a 67 mark last time, finishing fourth, and is now well treated at 66. Proven over this trip and ground, and the booking of Kieran O'Neill catches the eye. This drop into a slightly calmer contest gives every chance for this horse to convert late effort into a result.

EW CHANCE in this as he drops another 2 lb to a mark of 76, a mark he won off a year ago. Has possibly had training issues as he has only had a couple of runs this calendar year and has been off another 2 months+. However, he has won after a break previously and can go well here.
Not beaten far when third at Chelmsford last time out and has been placed twice in her three handicap starts. Can get a first success off an unchanged mark here.
Good Shot has been a bit down the pack for all runs so far, but she gets Oisin Murphy for this handicap debut, which makes me think that more is expected today.

Three career runs for the 3yo filly. Turf debut five weeks ago in a novice stakes, won by a smart front runner rated 80. The selection sat in second and was travelling better than the rest but probably paid the price for trying to match the winner and tired late on. Something to build on, still unexposed, an opening handicap mark of 53 looks attractive and she won’t be chasing an 80 rated runner in this 0-55 handicap.

I believe Walk the Moon has a chance here. Liking the turf and distance will suit. Oisin Murphy has a 25% strike rate here at Lingfield as well. A. Carroll has a respectable yard and performs well here also. E/W possibilities.
This horse is one of only two last time out winners and one of only two to have won at the 11.5f trip; should go well.

La Trinite: Not much to put here other than I have faith in this one turning into a nice one. It has a lot to find here, but it does look like an open race in which the top of the market is worth taking on. Hoping the transfer to turf and first-time cheek pieces can make a difference.
No new trainer bounce LTO when only 11 of 14 at Brighton back in April of this year. But now running off the lowest career mark and is helped by a drop down in class, so anything is possible.

The Initial Promise was validated by winning the 5-runner novice at Beverley 3 weeks ago, finishing impressively despite some mishaps. More progress is anticipated, and the 2-year-old has clear opportunities even with a penalty. The Scott yard is excelling, and jockey Shepherd has recorded 52 wins here in the last 5 seasons.

Command the Stars is unsurprisingly popular, but he didn't beat much on his debut. So Armstrong doesn't have to be special to win this. He's also entered in a Class 2 race in August, which clearly shows what connections think of him already.
At the weights, Delicatesse should get her first win on turf, having won here over 6f on the all-weather. She was a close 2nd over course and distance last August on similar going.

Twirling was rated thirty pounds higher than Hope Rising on the flat when trained by S & E Crisford. But now with Nicky Henderson, after an absence since October, she will have been well-schooled for her first hurdle race and should be fit enough to win.

The model I run suggests Squire Danagher can win this one. Squire Danagher lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 8-runner field but has been relatively well treated in the weights. The entire field is covered by an initial weight difference of 7 lbs. Squire Danagher ran a good second place 31 days ago and looks to go one better here. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Has his 2nd chase run, with Sean Bowen booked to ride again. If I'm honest, I expected better of him on chase debut. The market tended to agree with that theory, sent off 6/4 fav. He ran well but just couldn't match the finishing speed of the front two. To be fair, the winner made most of the running and was given a great ride. The second was given a good ride also. This fella was giving over a stone to both of those horses. You'd imagine this track will suit him better anyway. The trainer is 4-7 with his chasers at this track. Again, he's being run over a trip arguably short of ideal. He did win over this distance over hurdles and also based off his P2P run behind De Tellers Fortune. This trip is completely fine.

Sovereign Star, representing the Old Gold Racing Club, showed improvement last time to get his first win under Donald McCain. Though penalized 3lbs, he should still be competitive and can certainly be involved in the finish if running and jumping well here.

Rock House will like today's conditions and trip and is well capable of being in the mix. Dan Skelton has a 13.79% strike rate at this course. Came 4th last time out but jumped the last hurdle badly and lost 2nd position as a result. E/W ability.

The model I run suggests Isocrate can win this one. Isocrate lines up here with a comparably high RPR but has an official rating that leaves him well treated in the weights. Steps out carrying nearly a stone less than the top weight and current market leader Ballytechno. Has shown some form with figures of 48P-31 and the latest victory 3 days ago. Race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The Dream Goes On returned from a break in March to two wins at 2m3f but then fell. It took a run to get her confidence back, but she perked up last month and was just out of the money when 3/6 at 2m5f. She drops another couple of lbs and gets back to 2m4f, which could help bring her back in EW.

The model I run suggests De Tellers Fortune can win this one. De Tellers Fortune lines up here with the highest RPR of the 10-runner field but is not penalized for it in the weights. Has an official ranking that is second highest, but the entire field is largely well matched for weights. Form figures of 1P2P-1 with that last winner coming 52 days ago. Previous course winner and James Bowen picks up the reins. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator for this, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Sits just 3 lbs above his last winning mark. Returning to the scene of his sole chase win. Dropping back to the correct trip this time.
This is quite a competitive race for the grade. De Tellers Fortune and My Gift to You look big dangers but have questions to answer over this distance. Whereas this lad clearly thrives over a trip and boasts an unbeaten record at this track (2/2 here).
He absolutely battered the opposition when bolting up over CD back in November of last year, beating Sporting Ace by 15L, with My Gift to You beaten off in 3rd place.
Admittedly, the latter is better off at the weights with us this time. I don't think it's enough to overturn that huge CD defeat behind this fella. The first-time tongue tie is enlisted. Hopefully, that can unlock the required improvement to win this race.
Top combo in James Owen and Sam Twiston-Davies here. My Gift To You has looked good in this role and is improving with each outing. Placed in last two starts and looks hard to beat here.

Having triumphed at Bangor last June and being the runner-up on 7 occasions in 2024, he boosted his record by taking the lead in the 3m Ludlow handicap in April. Unfortunately, that race unraveled and predictably came up short at Stratford next time, competing off 5lb higher. With another chance at the handicap, jockey Paul O'Brien, who is performing exceptionally well, will be prepared. At 14/1, an each-way profit appears likely.
Has been in great form over both hurdles and fences, returning to the smaller obstacles here looking to achieve a hat-trick in a little over seven weeks.

Last run was a good one considering the saddle slipped between the last two jumps. The rider said he was unable to ride out fully to finish. Given the same mark today, a different result is expected as it has jumped up the ratings in the last seven runs, including four wins. 129 now from 102 sounds each way.

Earth King looked to be going well when stumbling and unseating the rider three out at Worcester. He comes back off a two-month break here, but his last run was off a 196-day break, so he is capable of running well off a break.

Put an end to a losing streak by taking charge just before the finish at Carlisle in April, but was outpaced in 2 subsequent higher class races. He is back on the same mark as his April win, but this race is tougher. Improvement is necessary with the new headgear, but Walford is focusing his efforts here, and it usually works out well when he sends just one runner to a hurdles meeting. The 14/1 odds seem like a solid option for an each-way bet in this case.
Fancy the Bowen double tomorrow. Only its second race with O Murphy, the Murphy/bowen combo round uttoxeter is solid. Well weighted. Gets the same conditions in which it's won it's only race.

The model I run suggests Getaway Jewel should win this one. Getaway Jewel lines up here with the second highest RPR fo this 10 runner field but has an offical raning which is third from bottom. subseqently goes out carrying over a stone less than the other market leaders. Has shown some decent form coming into this with figures of 5564-1 and needs to show more to chalk up another first place finish here. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Solid Fuel was 8 lb out of the handicap when not beaten far in 4th over 2m 1/2f on good ground at Worcester a fortnight ago. Was leading at the last, and all three in front were rated 108 or more. Gets in the handicap proper today with a drop in class. The 7-year-old likes a galloping track that he gets here. Won over 2m on good ground in June last year.

Crystal Mer had been placed on a couple of occasions for Paul Webber, including on his final start for them at Plumpton on May 24. He moved to Hughie Morrison and was backed off the boards on debut over course and distance last month, winning easily by 3 lengths. He is 10 lbs higher here, but with Sean Bowen again riding, he looks to have a great chance of following up.

Won at Cartmel last time out to make it eight wins in twenty-two career chases. Comes back to hurdling where the record is not as solid, but is 8 lb better off here and 6 lbs better than when 2nd here at Uttoxeter when hurdling before. Has also won on this ground more recently when chasing.

Ambassador, who was beaten 17 lengths by Crystal Mer last time over CD on good to soft, is a better horse on good ground (4 wins). He is 19 lbs better off today when the rider's 7 lb claim is also considered. He is somewhat of a track specialist with 4 wins and 3 frame finishes from 10 starts here. His last win came in July 2024 off an 11 lb higher mark, and he is capable of pushing the favorite all the way in this, with a better chance of reversing the form than the double-figure odds suggest.

Dan Skelton is very reliable in bumpers, and his Son of Tyran showed a lot of promise in his first outing under rules when just ran out of it in a three-way finish at Newton Abbot, with the first three well clear of the rest of the field. With improvement, he should go close here.

The model I run suggests Sevarana can win this one. Sevarana lines up here with the joint highest RPR of the 9-runner field but is not penalized for it in the weights. Most of these runners in this National Hunt Flat have only run one race before, and so experience is important in these kinds of races. A decent showing when 2nd last time out 44 days ago and should come on from that experience. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The 7yo lost his way last year but was back in form with a handicap win last week, after coming off a 6 month break. Big player at the weights in this low grade 0-50 classified stakes and he has been rated way higher in the past.

Voodoo Ray is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Gary & Josh Moore and has 5/21 wins, picking up three races last year under today's jockey, Tim Queally. He is a course specialist, winning four times at Brighton. This CD winner has won off marks of 46-49-50-55-58 and runs here in a classified stakes. He is a four-time winner on today's good ground, and while not coming here in the best of form, he has to be respected now back at Brighton. He runs well fresh, having won after a 169-day break last year at this track. Tim Queally rides Brighton well, picking up 8/9 winners in the last two years coming for Gary & Josh Moore. Voodoo Ray is a horse he knows well, winning on him 4/5 of his wins, and is my short-priced banker of the day.

Despite being labeled a poor performer lately, after being placed 6th in the Classified Stakes at this course and distance just a week ago, racing energetically before losing momentum. Nevertheless, this 6-year-old has valuable experience, and I wouldn't dismiss his chances of finishing in the top spots, especially at 40/1.

This D Loughnane-trained filly made a promising racecourse debut over seven furlongs on good to firm ground at Lingfield 17 days ago when beaten 1 1/2 lengths in second of the eight runners behind the W J Knight-trained True Test. With improvement likely after that run, she can go one place better tonight with Rossa Ryan booked to ride.

Hadn't won in 28 starts but seems to have turned a corner, winning his last 3 starts with the first two over course and distance. Now off a mark of 60 which is still workable, as he has run well off marks in the low 60s. Rossa Ryan in the plate makes the 4 timer quite possible.
Needs a strong pace to be seen to best effect and probably doesn't get that here. However, his record at Brighton reads 2/1/1, so worth a punt here.

Jazz Scene switched yards at the end of last year, and this will be the 3rd run for the new yard. He has not been unfancied in the last 2 runs, and his mark has slipped back to 62. He won off that mark about a year ago and can do so again today.

Winner over 5 and a half furlongs here at Brighton. This is over 6 and a half, and Ghiani is taking the mount for the first time and would have to be good enough against Time Patrol. SC Williams, the trainer, has an almost 19% strike rate at the track. The one with a win last time out.

George Boughey has Kranjcar representing his yard here, and with Pat Cosgrave in the saddle on a horse who is yet to finish out of the money in three runs here and as a course and distance winner, he looks a decent prospect.

The 4yo filly was too keen last time out but she has gone close twice this year, in her two races at this track. Still on a decent mark, suited by the quick ground, relatively unexposed after just six career runs and a very strong jockey change for this handicap.

Pit Boss, a 3-year-old grey gelding, ran poorly last time on soft going. Before that, at Goodwood, he performed to a certain level. Now 3 pounds lower in the handicap and down in grade, he is a speculative punt. Each way price.

This is one of the outsiders in this 8 runner race, but she gets 5lb and more from the rest of the field and could upset the hot favourite which is at the other end of the handicap. Her only run from 7 starts over this trip and ground was in a maiden where she was close enough to 70ish rated horses to suggest she could be worth giving another chance to here off 57. There's also an interesting angle on sire stats since progeny of the sire have won 4 from 10 at this very tricky course which is another potential positive.
Ran on well at Chepstow under Leavy (first time up). Distance is just a few more yards. Should improve on previous attempts over 7 furlongs, almost a mile.

United Force won at Southwell in December under Marco off a 50. He returned from a short break in April with the same rider and finished third off a 51. With another midfield run last time out on GS, he drops to a 49 and could be ready to strike again with the return of Marco.

Headshot who is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Tony Carroll and ridden by Holly Doyle. He is a four-time winner but just 1/19 on turf. He sports a first-time visor today, and when Tony Carroll does and Holly rides, he is 1/3 wins, winning with Madrhino at 14-1 in a first-time hood/visor. Holly is 7/18 wins on Carroll's older horses, 7/8-year-olds in class 6 events, so Holly gets a good tune out of Carroll's older horses. He is a four-time winner over today's trip, and whilst finishing well down the field last time out behind an 8- length winner, Cloudy Rose, it was an inadequate 12f, and he took a keen hold and weakened under an inexperienced amateur. He drops back down to a mile today, which will evidently suit on past form. Whilst it's good ground today, it's likely to dry out due alto favorable weather and handles good to firm ground, winning at Bath and has posted an RPR of 67 at Brighton to boot. Holly is also 22/106 wins for Tony Carroll in class 6 races if 14-1 or less since 2015. A distinct possibility of a win despite not being too well found in the market.
Started this year winning at Southwell, but form has been poor since then and only has 3 wins from 33 runs, which is shocking. Hopefully, the time off does him some good.

This J R Fanshawe-trained 3-year-old gelding has won once over seven furlongs on good ground at Epsom and has been placed second in three of his last five races. The latest was over seven furlongs on good ground at Haydock when only beaten 3/4 length behind the Rae Guest-trained Sunlit Uplands, despite finding trouble in running. So with Kyle Strydon back onboard, it looks like a win tonight.

Seo Linn was a winner of three bumpers, including at Listed and Grade 2 level. Switching to the flat this season, starting in maidens, she has finished 3rd and 4th in her first two races. With Colin Keane up, she should get her first win over 12f here at Tramore.
There are a few with good chances in this race, and I am going to side with Make Good, who has been a little inconsistent, but whose best form has come over this trip and at his level.

It has been 16 runs since her last win in 2024. A solid 2nd place in a handicap at Roscommon just 7 days ago, finishing with a strong push. If the 4-year-old can handle a longer trip, she could perform admirably again, and jockey Shane Foley will have that all figured out.
Won well at Brighton last time out on the flat and had a warm-up over hurdles when seventh at Tipperary last week. Should be all the better for that appearance.

Anjah has not run on turf that many times in recent years but finally won on the all-weather at Dundalk last September, which pushed his all-weather mark to 49. However, after poor runs at Sligo before that run and after a 226-day break in May, his turf mark has dropped to only 42. Nicola Burns takes off another seven pounds. He could leave his previous turf form behind.
A tricky little handicap where a chance is taken on Arthur's Victory, who at 25/1 looks great value. He ran well recently over jumps and looks well handicapped back on the flat.

Lord Erskine despite being a twelve year old is still going strong winning his latest race at Fairyhouse in April in a Listed handicap hurdle. His last flat win was in September 2023 at the Curragh over two miles and one furlong off his current mark of 79 and Nicola Burns takes the ride taking off seven pounds.

Drop The Anchor brings solid hurdle form into this staying Flat handicap and has shaped as though this kind of test would suit. Still well handicapped on old ratings and stays 2m+ well. Trainer looks to be in decent form and this looks winnable if he settles early. Proven stayer dropping in class, worth a second look.
Won a couple of flat races over a slightly shorter trip. Comes from a top Irish stable and off this mark can get involved. Ground will suit.
